[18] Further, embedded part probing and tool setting features available on most modern CNC equipment are highly useful to ensure part location/orientation and cutting tool location and form are known prior cutting the workpiece. For large piece parts exceeding 1.5m or so, large format gantry machines can be utilized such as the GM-2- 5AX. The GM-2-5AX is a full 5-axis “gimbal head” machine, where both rotary axes are mounted on the Z- axis ram, and the spindle/cutting tool assembly rotates, while the workpiece is stationary on the machine table. This allows the cutting tool to point at any angle within the rotary-axis travel limits. This style of machine requires more facility particulate and temperature environmental controls due to its open topology, along with stiffer foundations to manage the higher loads and lower resonant frequencies. These factors will significantly add to the infrastructure and capex costs during factory setup and thus the choice to constrain the OAL to ~1m is prudent. The machine’s rigid steel construction provides a very stable cutting platform, and a 1" thick aluminum table is standard. Therefore, following critical machining operations it is important to perform measurements of the mechanical features generated and to ensure that other critical dimensions were not affected by fixturing or cutting forces. Although some features may be inspected through the use of conventional manual inspection tools such as micrometers, gauge pins and various indicator setups, complex geometries and numerous geometries are best inspected through the use of coordinate measuring machines (CMMs). The most frequently utilized types of CMMs within the accelerator manufacturing industry are Bridge CMMs, Cantilever CMMs and laser trackers. Figure 11: Bridge CMM (left), Cantilever CMM (center) and laser tracker CMM (right). The most precise and accurate CMMs tend to be in the bridge CMM category due to their rigid platforms, thermal compensation systems and sensitive probing options. For example in the fabrication of CLIC structures at CERN, bridge CMMs were utilized including a Leitz® PMM-C Infinity with a measuring error of MPEE [μm] = 0.3 + L/1000 (L in [mm]), a probing error MPEP [μm] = 0.4 and a scanning probing error MPETHP [μm] = 1.2 / 59 [s] according to ISO 10360-2 and ISO 10360-4 respectively [18].
